text:
maya: quick sync — I ran an apples-vs-replay comparison for the /embed-rerank endpoint. goal: understand tail behavior across batching heuristics, kernel selection, and KV warm/cold effects. artifacts: <https://artifacts/redwood/bench/1792504321>

maya: brief setup: replay harness (prod traces, anonymized) vs synthetic (zipf session generator). models: rerank-bert-like variants at dims 256/512/1024. payloads: 1..50 candidates per req. qps sweep: 50/200/500. batchers: fixed(max_batch=64) and adaptive(latency SLO 80ms). kernels: fp16 native, int8 quant, and fallback generic kernel. KV cache: warm vs cold passes.

maya: example command I used:
```bash
./bench --mode replay --trace traces/2026-03-10.json --qps 200 \
  --batcher adaptive --max-batch 64 --model rerank-512 --quant fp16 --kv-cache on
```

omar: can you drop the p50/p95/p99 for dim=512 qps=200? also which hw? :thinking_face:

maya: hw: g5x2 equiv (A100-ish), single-shard per worker. results (512, qps=200, adaptive): p50=9ms, p95=41ms, p99=178ms (warm KV). cold-KV p99 ballooned to ~420ms for same run.

sasha: that cold->warm delta is huge. was KV warming sequential or parallel during replay? could be KV cache write lock causing cascade.

maya: replay preserves original arrival order, so KV warms gradually — the heavy tail aligns with early sessions where many large candidates cause cache churn. profiler shows a hotspot around the KV lookup path + a kernel fallback.

maya: profiler snippet:
```
HOT: aten_mm_fp16_fused           42% CPU (small GEMMs)
FALLBACK: aten_mm_generic         18% CPU (triggered for seq_len>1024)
KV_LOOKUP: shard_kv_get_batch     12% CPU (locks + memcpy)
```

ed: interesting about the fallback — is the kernel selector using seq_len cutoff? we pushed a selector rule change yesterday that prefers fused kernels only up to 1024, otherwise generic. maybe that interacts with batching producing longer sequences.

jen: flagged infra change: kernel-selector v1.4 deployed 1792500000 — rolling back to v1.3 on a canary now because we saw perf alerts. will report if rollback changes tail.

perf-bot: artifacts uploaded: <https://artifacts/redwood/bench/1792504321/logs.tar.gz> and flamegraphs at <https://artifacts/redwood/bench/1792504321/flame.html>

omar: did you try pinning the kernel to force fused for those sequences just to see if fallback is the root cause?

maya: yes — pinned fused kernel for all seq_len and rerun (same qps). p99 improved from 178ms -> 95ms (warm KV). so kernel fallback explains ~50% of tail. remaining delta is KV behavior + batching spikes.

sasha: how did adaptive batcher compare to fixed max_batch=64? which one caused more long sequences?

maya: fixed-64 produced bigger avg batch sizes and slightly lower p50 (7ms) but p99 was worse (230ms) because occasional huge batches forced fallback due to seq_len combined with padding.

ed: sounds like we need two levers: 1) smarter kernel selector that considers padding overhead and batch composition, 2) batcher heuristic to cap padding inflation (e.g., prefer smaller batch if padding ratio > 0.6). can we add a metric for padding ratio per batch in CI?

maya: agreed. I added a new metric in the harness: batch_padding_ratio and batch_seq_variance. example log line:
```
BATCH_METRIC: size=48 pad_ratio=0.67 seq_var=320
```

jen: after rolling back kernel-selector, do we want to land the padding guard and a canary for kernel pinning? ops prefers kernel pin pinned for 24h while we iterate on batcher heuristics.

maya: proposed action items:
- reproduce with pinned/kernel selector off (maya) :white_check_mark:
- add padding_ratio alert to perf CI (ed)
- add warm-vs-cold KV test in replay harness and add KV-hit-rate baseline to dashboards (sasha)
- run full qps sweep with int8 quant and synthetic harness to validate apples-to-apples vs replay (maya)

ed: I'll add the CI metric and a tiny fuzz test that generates pathological padding shapes.

sasha: I'll instrument KV path to report lock contention and per-shard miss rate. we should also test multi-shard sharding strategy — current single-shard gets overloaded under replay bursts.

maya: one last note — synthetic vs replay differences: synthetic had lower p99 by ~25% at same mean qps because it distributes candidate sizes more regularly. replay has burstiness and candidate-rich sessions that expose both KV coldness and kernel fallback. keep both harnesses in the perf checklist.

omar: +1. nice diagnostics. can you drop a one-pager summary into the perf wiki and tag infra + runtime? :thumbsup:

maya: will do. summary + artifacts link in the wiki. thanks everyone.
